correctness.rationale: For all k>=1 and odd primes p<q, multiplicativity gives a=M(p+1)-(p-M)q and a<Mp. A bounded representation a=r+sp+tq would force semiperfectness by binary block decomposition. Lemma 1 proves q>2M by an exact quotient/remainder and reallocation from p to q. Lemma 2 proves a<(p-M-1)q by pigeonholing p-M distinct residues into a space with only p-M-1 forbidden remainders. Splitting x=p-M at M/3 yields strict a<(2/3)M^2+M. The lower bound a>M is cited from Iannucci. Independent finite corroboration: 29,490 candidate pairs through k=8 with exact output.

value.rationale: This unrestricted strict abundance estimate advances a named open quantitative problem on primitive weird numbers, reducing the proved asymptotic coefficient from three quarters to two thirds, across all exponents and prime pairs. The result depends on substantive semiperfectness obstructions and is not a finite-range extrapolation, routine renaming, or arbitrary new parameter slice; its bound remains weaker than the one-third-scale conjecture.
